facts.text: Shelby Charter Township is in western Macomb County, bordered on the west by Rochester and Rochester Hills in Oakland County and on the south by Utica and Sterling Heights.
The township's two main thoroughfares are M-53, commonly called Van Dyke Avenue, and M-59, commonly called Hall Road.
The Shelby Township Civic Center Campus, home to Township Hall, the Shelby Township Library and Heritage Lake, sits at 24 Mile Road and Van Dyke Avenue.
The Shelby Township Downtown Development Authority district takes in all business locations along Van Dyke Avenue from the Utica border north to 26 Mile Road.
Christmas Aglow, an annual celebration on the Civic Center Campus, lights the township's 40-foot Christmas tree with a drone show and adds free photos with Santa, hayrides and festive music.
River Bends Park, more than 850 acres, is divided into two sections by the Clinton River, with the main entrance to its eastern section at 5700 22 Mile Road.
The Macomb Orchard Trail, a 24-mile hike and bike path, begins at 24 Mile Road and Dequindre in Shelby Township and runs northeast to the City of Richmond.
A small portion of Stony Creek Metropark extends into Shelby Township.
The Packard Proving Grounds, established in the township by the Packard Motor Car Company in 1927, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Shelby Township, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Christmas light installation for Shelby Township homes: rooflines, tall evergreens and shrubs, hung from bucket trucks. Free estimates.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Shelby Township, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Straight rooflines, wrapped evergreens and lit front walks, installed from bucket trucks where it counts and removed once the holidays wrap up.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Each year Christmas Aglow lights Shelby Township's 40-foot tree on the Civic Center Campus, with a drone show to go with it. Your house can have its own sense of occasion without the drones. We start with the roofline and entry, then look at what else earns light: a tall spruce by the drive, a row of shrubs along the walk, a pair of trees framing the front door. High peaks and tall evergreens are handled from a bucket truck where there is room for it. You get design, installation, in-season service and takedown after the holidays from us, start to finish.
considerations: A two-story peak or a tall spruce is where a ladder job shows: runs sag and spacing drifts. From a bucket truck, the crew can hang the top of the line as evenly as the bottom. At the estimate we check the ground, what is overhead and where the truck can set up.

If your subdivision has an association, check its guidelines on exterior decorations before install day. Our estimate describes what goes where, which makes any approval request simple to put together and easy for a board to review.

A display that stops at the gutter leaves the yard dark. Wrapped foundation shrubs and a lit front walk tie the house to the ground and light the way to the door for guests. We plan these low runs along with the roofline, so the whole display comes on together.
faq: Do you serve all of Shelby Township?

Yes. Shelby Township is in our service area, and so are nearby Rochester Hills and Macomb Township. Give us a call at (248) 756-8915, or use the request form on this page, and a free estimate will be arranged at a time that suits you.
Can you light a tall evergreen in the yard?

Usually. A tall evergreen can take a spiral wrap, which traces its shape, or strands run down from the top, which read as a softer cone of light. We look at the height and spread during the estimate and suggest the look that suits the tree and the rest of the display.
Do you take the lights down too?

Yes. Every seasonal display includes takedown after the holidays. Crews remove the strands and clips from the roofline, trees and shrubs, and takedown is listed in the estimate alongside design, installation and in-season service, so it is part of the plan from the first visit.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Shelby Township, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Commercial holiday lighting in Shelby Township for Van Dyke businesses, shopping centers, offices and HOA entrances. Outlines, pole decor and tree wraps.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Shelby Township, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Building outlines, tree wraps, pole decor and entrance displays for businesses along Van Dyke, plus offices, shopping centers and HOA entrances across the township.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Van Dyke Avenue and Hall Road are Shelby Township's two main thoroughfares, and the township's Downtown Development Authority district covers every business location along Van Dyke from the Utica border north to 26 Mile Road. In December it is dark before most people head home from work, so a business on that corridor is judged by what it looks like under headlights. A lit building outline, wrapped trees at the entrance and decorated light poles in the lot tell drivers you are open and ready for the season. Our plan starts at the road and works back to the door. Crews install from bucket trucks, we service the display through the holidays, and everything comes down after the season.
considerations: Lamppost and pole decor carries a theme across a lot and guides drivers to the door. We match the pole pieces to the building outline and entry trees, so the lot, the entrance and the building look like one design from the road.

Shopping centers and office parks need one look across many storefronts. We design the center as a whole, from the main sign to the last tenant's door, and schedule installation around store hours, deliveries and the busiest parts of the day.

For an HOA, the entrance carries the whole neighborhood's first impression. We light the sign, the plantings around it and any trees or islands at the entry, and plan around the power available at the monument.
faq: Do you light businesses along Van Dyke and Hall Road?

Yes. Both corridors are within our service area. We begin with a free walkthrough of the building, the lot, power and lift access. The written estimate that follows covers design, installation, in-season service and removal.
When should a shopping center or office book?

Late summer is not too soon. A multi-tenant property may need sign-off from the owner, the manager and sometimes the tenants, and each step takes time. Starting then lets approvals happen without squeezing the install, and booking earlier gives you more dates to choose from.
Can you wrap the trees along our frontage?

Usually. Frontage trees are what drivers see first, so they are often worth wrapping even when the building outline stays simple. At the walkthrough we look at each tree's height, how far it sits from power and where a bucket truck can work, then include the ones worth lighting in the estimate.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Lighting in Shelby Township, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Shelby Township permanent lighting: app-controlled roofline scenes for Christmas, team colors and everyday accent light, with no ladder season.
permanent-lighting.h1: Permanent Lighting in Shelby Township, MI
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: A roofline that changes with a tap. Christmas scenes in December, team colors on game day, warm accent light on every ordinary night.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: Permanent lighting ends the yearly routine of hanging lights each fall and taking them down in the January cold. A discreet track mounts under the eaves and stays put through winter and summer alike, while an app decides what it shows. Pick colors, save scenes and set schedules: a full Christmas look in December, orange in October, team colors on game day, and a warm white outline the rest of the time. The layout is planned around your roofline, and the app is set up with you once the lights are in.
considerations: Two-story homes with several gables are where an outline most often looks broken. We measure every peak and valley, then lay out the runs so the line climbs and drops with the roof, and the estimate shows how the second story and the garage roof connect.
Match the light to the house

Brick, stone and pale siding each change how a lit outline reads at night. During the estimate we look at your exterior and talk through which shade of white and which holiday colors suit it, so the scenes you save in the app look right from the street.

The system needs a power connection, and where it goes matters for looks and for access. At the estimate we pick a spot that keeps the connection out of sight from the street yet easy to reach, and mark it on the layout.
faq: Can I switch back to plain white after the holidays?
Yes. Switching scenes takes a tap in the app, so the roofline can go from a full Christmas display to a plain warm white outline the day after the holidays, then to team colors for the next big game.
Is my roofline a good fit?

Most rooflines are. Ranches with long, simple eaves are the most straightforward, and a two-story front with several peaks simply takes more measuring. If part of the roof is hidden by trees or faces a direction no one sees, the estimate leaves it out.
How do I get started in Shelby Township?

Use the request form on this page or call (248) 756-8915 with your address. We set a time to see the house, then send a free written estimate showing where the track runs on each side and spelling out what the installation includes.
